A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMOS framework and Habitat-MAS benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on 519 Habitat-MAS episodes, including component ablations, success rates, token usage, and sub-goal analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds empirical comparisons of resume formats and scalability with robot and object counts.

M1.justification: URDF-derived JSON resumes, numerical capability checks, centralized assignment and reflection, and decentralized execution remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Appendix A.2 expands the communication explanation; the format experiments do not replace the proposed method's JSON representation.

E1.justification: The HSSD/Matterport3D coverage and four benchmark tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C.6 adds manipulation scenarios with homogeneous Fetch teams and varying object loads, modestly extending the tested team composition and task complexity.

E2.justification: The original three component-ablation comparators remain unchanged. Table 4 adds natural-language, Markdown, and XML resume variants compared with the standard JSON choice. Newly cited systems such as HMAS-2 are not added as evaluated external baselines.

E3.justification: The original 519-episode, May-2024 GPT-4o evaluation remains unchanged. New protocols use ten perception episodes for format comparisons, with prompt adjustments, and ten manipulation episodes for robot-count comparisons. Object-count experiments hold the team at two Fetch robots.

E4.justification: Appendices C.5-C.6 add substantial new analysis areas: sensitivity to resume format and scalability with robot number and object load. These extend the original component ablations, token-efficiency analysis, sub-goal analysis, and hallucination case study, all of which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly stated ten-episode sample sizes do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and Figure 5 retain their results. New Tables 4-6 substantially extend the findings: format success rates are 0.3, 0.7, 0.5, and 0.6 for natural language, JSON, Markdown, and XML. Success rates for 2, 4, 6, and 10 robots are 80%, 60%, 70%, and 50%; increasing objects from one to five changes success from 90% to 70% and token usage from 25,778 to 197,485. These are results under added settings.

T1.justification: The policy, scene-graph, episode, and sub-goal definitions are retained, as are the camera-FOV and navigation-distance equations. No new or revised theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: EMOS, self-generated embodiment-aware robot resumes, Habitat-MAS, and evidence supporting numerical reasoning and group discussion. The additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The new appendix discussion recommends structured JSON resumes and identifies format-related action failures. It interprets scaling difficulties through context length and hallucinations, suggesting stronger models or subgroup communication. The earlier spatial-reasoning failure analysis remains.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2 and B.4 expand communication and control documentation, including greedy navmesh waypoint navigation and explicitly disabled collision detection during arm control. The abstract adds a project-site pointer. These clarify implementation and access information without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through heterogeneous-team learning, communication, task allocation, and swarm research, including Seraj, Bettini, and Ravichandar. It distinguishes EMOS through use of pretrained knowledge without additional training. Appendix A.2 newly attributes the communication design to Chen et al.'s HMAS-2, while several earlier planning references are removed.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the appendix into EMOS, benchmark, and experimental sections, and moves detailed planning/execution prose from Section 3.4 to Appendix A.2. Related-work headings, local prose, affiliations, and corresponding-author information are edited; most existing narrative remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the communication diagram in Figure 7 and compact result Tables 4-6. Existing displays are retained and repositioned, including Table 1 and Algorithm 1; the original case-study Figure 7 becomes Figure 8. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution and implementation transparency and adds useful evidence about resume formatting and scalability in Appendices C.5-C.6. The gains are limited: the format and robot-count studies use ten episodes, prompt modifications are unspecified, and uncertainty estimates remain absent. The core method and original empirical evidence are preserved.
